ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle block move
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, The Navigation and Administration blocks are no longer used in recent versions of Moodle. Navigation is provided by the course index and administration links are in the course navigation, both of which are always in the same place and can't be moved. Thus, if you can upgrade to a supported version of Moodle, the navigation and administration will no longer be movable. Alternatively, you can make blocks sticky as described in the documentation Block settings .

ResponsesInList.Title: Students role with and without self-enroll permission
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle, I would like to achieve the following setup: Have default student accounts (users) who have the ability to self-enroll in courses. Have external user accounts that cannot self-enroll but can be manually enrolled into specific courses by management. Is there a way to configure Moodle to accommodate these two different user enrollment scenarios? We have 'normal' students that follow the whole program, and external students that only follow one course - and they shouldn't be able to view other course content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students role with and without self-enroll permission
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christiaan, To prevent external students from being able to self-enrol, you need to edit the Authenticated user role and unset the capability to self enrol in courses (enrol/self:enrolself). To enable default students to self-enrol, you need to create a new 'Self-enroller' role with the capability to self enrol in courses allowed. Select 'System' as context type where the role may be assigned and then assign all your default students this role as a system role (via Site admin > Users > Assign system roles ). Your default students will then have the Self-enroller role and also the role of student when they self-enrol in courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students role with and without self-enroll permission
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, that is a solution that works for me!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students role with and without self-enroll permission [Solved]
ResponsesInList.Text: Good to hear that my suggested solution works for you Christiaan. Thanks for letting us know! An alternative solution for if you have fewer external students would be to leave the capability to self enrol allowed for the Authenticated user role, create a new 'Unable to self enrol' role with the capability to self enrol prohibited and assign this role to your external students as a system role.

ResponsesInList.Title: Group Permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Currently I have a structure in Moodle that could be considered “unfeasible” and I would like some light to know the best choices I can make. Whenever the school year begins, I replicate my clients' courses, including creating courses for each class. For example: a school with 1st and 2nd year, and each year with 2 classes: there would be 4 courses. This becomes unfeasible for many clients because it weighs a lot on my system, in addition to being a bit annoying to duplicate courses. It was then that I did some research and found the groups option in Moodle. I carried out some tests and I have some doubts about how I can apply this without having problems. 1- When applying the group system to a course, do I have a guarantee that teachers will only have access to registered groups? (of course, with the course/moodle's internal permissions configured for this). 2- Regarding reports/report plugins, is this grouping problem normally resolved? 3- Is there a facilitator to register users and teachers separated by groupings? Also, is this group option the best way to separate my clients on a large scale? Hope i'm not on the wrong topic Thank you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group Permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gustavo, You can indeed make it so that teachers can only access students in their groups. For details of how to set it up, see the FAQ 'How do I restrict a teacher to view only information about the groups that they are in?' in Groups FAQ . Teachers will only be able to access reports of students in their groups for reports in standard Moodle. For any additional report plugins, you would need to check. A facilitator or other user with a role in which the manage groups capability is allowed, and the access all groups capability is not set, is able to add/delete/update groups in a course. As for the best way to separate clients on a large scale, as well as considering whether to use courses or groups, another possibility is using Multi-tenancy , though this is only available in Moodle Workplace .

ResponsesInList.Title: Restrict non-editing teacher's ability to see info outside of its group?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm looking for recommendations on an approach to limit what information a non-editing teacher can view in a course in Moodle 4.4.1. Background We are selling access to a course built in our Moodle LMS. We are using a single course for all customers/schools. In the course we have applied the following settings: Group mode: Separate groups Force group mode: Yes Default grouping : None At this time, we are only supporting self-enrollment using an enrollment key. We create a new Self-enrolment enrollment method for each school that purchases access. Here are some of the key properties we are utilizing: Custom instance name: School name Allow new self enrolments: Yes Enrolment key: we generate a unique key and enter it here Use group enrolment keys: Yes Default assigned role: Student Max enrolled users: we set to the number of users purchased Next we create a new group in the course for the school. Here are the key properties we are utilizing: Group name: School name Enrolment key: same key that was generated for the Enrolment key Group membership visibility: Only see own membership or Hidden So far this is working well for us. We are able to provide each school with their unique enrollment key and when users enroll, they are automatically added to the group. From my testing so far, this has been sufficient to ensure students can't find students from other course groups. For additional context , we have comments, discussions, and messaging disabled so there's really no need for students to find each other. What we desire Next we want to figure out how to get the teacher into the course. The primary purpose for this is so that the teacher can track student progress and to view students' grades. The teacher does not need much else and does not need to be able to edit grades. The assumption is that if the teacher wants to utilize the grade results from this course, they will have to manually copy them over to their own system (until next year when we get LTI with grade sync working). Requirements: A teacher can be added to the course as a non-editing teacher or similar custom role The teacher can view their students in the course participants section, but filtered to just the students in their group regardless of the selected filter The teacher can view the gradebook, but is limited to only the grades of the users in their school's group The teacher can not find any data from users of a different group A single course is used for all schools As you can infer, we are trying to answer data privacy concerns before we allow teacher roles in the course. I'm looking for validation that this is achievable and that I'm not missing anything obvious from my initial testing mentioned below. Questions Is it possible to restrict the data a user can view by a group? Is this actually the default behavior in moodle when using Separate group mode? I tested this by creating a group and enrolling 1 teacher and 1 student in the same group. There are other participants in the course too. When I signed in as the teacher and viewed participants, my view was automatically filtered by my group. I then removed my group filter and applied changes. Interestingly, I still only see users in my group. I then went to the gradebook and I again only see users in my group and I don't see a way to remove the filter here. If this seems like asking too much out of Moodle, what would you recommend to achieve similar functionality? We are trying hard to avoid duplicating courses for this school year. Is it possible to create one self-enrollment key used for students and another used for teachers that both enroll into the same course and group but with different roles? How does a user manually enroll in a group using a group key? I assume this must be possible somehow, but I haven't seen a place a user can go to join a group manually. What gotchas and downsides will we run into with this methodology?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict non-editing teacher's ability to see info outside of its group?
ResponsesInList.Text: Regarding restricting a teacher's ability to only see their group - please see the documentation Groups FAQ and the specific question How do I restrict a teacher to view only the information about the groups they are in? Regarding adding a teacher to a group manually, assuming they have an account on the site, go go the course as admin, click Participants in the course navigation and click  the Enrol users button and enrol them as non-editing teacher - and then from the dropdown on the left, click Groups and manually move them from the box on the right to the correct group on the left. An alternative if you want them to self enrol is to set up self enrolment with a group enrolment key but make the 'Default assigned role' non-editing teacher (yes you can do this, when you access the self-enrolment settings)  and only tell the teacher that group enrolment key - otherwise students could enrol themselves as non-editing teachers instead of students.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles Library
ResponsesInList.Text: At the open university, we have over 50 custom roles, so I am not going to give a complete list, but some examples: We have roles allocated in the system context, to identify people as either staff or students. (When stuff study a course, they get a different roles for that.) We aucutally have a several of student roles for enrolling people in courses, becuase of our system of making courses read-only once they are finished. So we have Full students = Student (read-only) + Contributing student. And, similarly, we have several variants of editing / non-editing teacher, giving various levels of access to different people. Various site-wide roles for who need to access most courses (helpdesk, assessment admin, course setup admin, ...) Various roles we can use to prohibit things like posting to forums/blogs/wikis, so if someone is being naghty we can temporarily stop then posting, until we can reached out to them, and resolved the issue. Various technical roles, to control access to particular web services we have to let other systems integrate with our Moodle in a controlled way. And so on... Some of these roles are automatically allocated by our data integrations, some of them are allocated manually. Overall, Moodle's roles system is essential for how we run our site.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles Library
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Tim. Thanks for the role descriptions. Item #5 caught my attention. Could you give us an example, forum perhaps, of the permissions that need to be prohibited? Ricardo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles Library
ResponsesInList.Text: To give one example: there is a 'Restrict forum' role, which prohibits all the capabilities that students have to post in forums. If you assign that at site level, then the student cannot post in any forum anywhere in the system.. So, if you get reports that a particular user is abusing the system, you can quickly assign that role, so they cannot post any more. Then the situation is contained while you contact them, investigate what is or is-not happening, and make an appropriate response. Once the situation is resolved, then you can un-assign the 'Restrict forum' role, and all their permissions are back to normal. This is a very rare occurrence, but with 100,000+ users, it happens occasoinally.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cohort

You could create a Teacher A , B, etc role that has the permissions you want them to have and assign the teachers to that role in categories (if you made it a category role) or at the site level. I'm not giving them site permissions. But they need to see their employees. I assign all employees to a group and I add a non-editing teacher role to that administrator and make sure he or she is assigned to the group. Now he/she sees their employees and no one else. They can't change my course. They can't change grades. They can see their staff, reports on their staff, the grades for their staff. Is this what you are looking for?

ResponsesInList.Title: New limited admin user permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I am hoping that someone in the community can help with this issue please. We have created a new more limited Admin role for our organisation.  The general purpose of this role is to view delegates' progress and this has been working well, as they don't get all of the Site Admin menus and can't accidentally change anything. However, we have now a hidden activity in a course that we would like this limited Admin role to mark as complete when an external condition is met. We have added a condition in the completion settings to say that this activity needs to be marked as complete (as well as the other grading conditions) before the course is complete.  (This new hidden activity has been added as a label, but if anyone has any other thoughts about how this could be better achieved, please let me know!) As a full Moodle Administrator, I can mark this activity as complete by turning editing on and then navigating to the student's course completion report and then tick the label activity for the relevant student.  I can then see this checked off in the course completion report.  So far, so good. The problem arises for the limited Admin role that we have created because they cannot turn editing on, so cannot mark the label activity as complete.  In the role settings, the 'manually mark activities as complete' is set to 'allow', so I don't know why this role is not able to manually mark this activity as complete. Does anyone know what I can do to allow this limited Administrator to mark this activity as completed please? Also, any thoughts on whether this label activity method works best, or if there may be better alternatives. Many thanks. Tracy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New limited admin user permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Tracy, The capability 'Manually mark activities as complete' is what allows students to mark an activity complete for themselves. The capability "Mark users as complete in course completion" does what you need: https://docs.moodle.org/400/en/Course_completion_settings#Condition:_Manual_completion_by_others .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New limited admin user permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Randy, Thanks for your post and the link. I am still stuck. Please see attached Custom Role permissions.  These are the permissions for a user who has been assigned this custom role, from a course level perspective.  I have highlighted a few permissions that may be relevant. The context types where this role may be assigned is 'system', 'category' and 'course'.  Is this right for my purposes? The main issue is that I still don't understand why this custom admin user cannot mark the activities as completed. Any further pointers would be appreciated. Tracy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New limited admin user permissions
ResponsesInList.Text:
Ah, now I see. So, you want them to mark the activity on the Activity completion report. The role will need at least these two Allowed: View activity completion reports - report/progress:view Override activity completion status - moodle/course:overridecompletion because what is actually happening on that page is making completion overrides. Manager, Teacher and Non-editing teacher have that Allowed by default. If they are only doing this by using the report, then they don't need
the manage permissions to turn on editing. They should be able to do the
overrides in the report. At least, that did work for me in 3.11 with overriding a Label. You may also need to allow them to see hidden things as well since the Labels are hidden: View hidden activities - moodle/course:viewhiddenactivities View hidden sections - moodle/course:viewhiddensections Though perhaps not if the view permission on the report is sufficient. The context for this needs only to be Course, since the report belongs to the course. Try it with and without actually enrolling the users with that role in the courses. The Manager role can do such overrides and it does not need to be enrolled in the course, so - in theory - it should work either way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New limited admin user permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Randy, I really appreciate you looking into this. I had already set 'View activity completion reports - report/progress:view' to allow, but had missed the 'Override activity completion status - moodle/course:overridecompletion' permission, so I changed that to 'allow' today. Now everything is working perfectly! I really appreciate your help with this. Thank you. Regards, Tracy

ResponsesInList.Title: Bulk creation of roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, If we want to create a role based on existing student role, we usually create a new role manually from site Administration. Is there a way that we can create more than one role in bulk (may be as CSV) based on existing student role arch type?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk creation of roles
ResponsesInList.Text: No, there is no not. There is no way do this in bulk via a csv because there would be too many fields since a role can have hundreds of settings and it is not common to need to create so many roles. Instead, you can use the export function to save a role as a "role preset" xml file, then import it to make a new role. If you really want to do this outside of Moodle, you can directly edit the xml file to change things like its shortname and other settings but it will probably not save you any more work than doing that part manually in the interface.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I get Teacher Profile to Show on course Page?
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to go into the Site admin > Plugins > Filters and then enable it in the filter list. I usually put it second in the list so that it processes early. It is a filter, so it is reading the text on the page as the is being sent to the user and replacing the variables with the actual values. The list of the all the variables it supports are on the Plugin documentation page: https://moodle.org/plugins/filter_filtercodes . It uses curly braces {} for the variables. For example, create a Label in a course and enter this: Hello (firstname}! Welcome to {coursename}. Save it and then log in as a student to the course. When the page loads, the filter will replace {firstname} and {coursename} with the proper values of that user and that course. You will find many more examples for how to use it in this forum: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=359252

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing student blogs - what role ?
ResponsesInList.Text: The Manager role should be able to do this. It has the capabilities "Edit and manage entries moodle/ blog :manageentries" and "View all user blogsmoodle/user:readuserblogs" set to Allow. If you don't want to give those users all the abilities of the Manager, you can create a new System level role which just the permissions needed for the blogs. You can find all of them in the definition of the Manager role. (As in the screenshot). You may need to experiment with exactly which of those permissions you need to add. This would allow all such users who have that role to see all user blogs. You may or may not be able to get this to also work by adding those directly to the Teacher role. Teachers are only teachers however inside courses and blogs are not in courses, they are at the system and user context , not the course one. So, it may not be possible to limit which teachers see which student blogs. In any case, experimenting with those capabilities is the way to find out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing student blogs - what role ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Julien, Interesting. I am not sure that it would be possible to create a blog entry using another user's id as the creator. When you create it, Moodle assigns it to the user who created it. (This is the same with forum posts, too.). For admins, they can use the "Log in as" another user to create the blog as another user. You can assign this permission to other roles, it's "Login as other users moodle/user:loginas". There's a lot of security implications if you do that, of course. There are no standard notifications for blogs, but there are some events for them. You may be able to set up an Event monitoring notification for such events. Take a look in Site admin > Reports > Event monitoring rules. I am pretty sure at least blog entry creation and deletion are covered, but I am not sure about comments.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can Teachers only see specific Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Users can not go into courses they are not assigned to or enroled in (in some way). Users can see inside and edit courses where they are enroled as Teachers. Users assigned as system level Managers can see inside and edit all courses in the site without being directly enroled in them. If you assign the same person as Manager to courses AND also as Teacher as courses, then they have two roles, with the combined power of those roles. If you want some users to be only Teachers in their courses, and not edit other courses they are not Teachers in, then do not make them Managers: only enrol them in the relevant courses as Teachers. You might take a look at the documentation that explains this in more detail.

If you want Teacher/Managers "to only be able to see certain Courses and users in those courses" then enrol them as a Teacher in the courses they need, but do not give them the Manager role too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cohort manager role
ResponsesInList.Text: If you create a category for each school and put the courses in the relevant category, all you need to do is give a person Manager permission at the category level (not site). Build the cohort in the category. The manager will have all permissions for those courses and none for courses in any other category. If you don't want them to have specific permissions, you can probably copy the manager role at the site level, rename it (cohort manager), and remove any of the permissions you don't want them to have.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have a  issue on a Moodle 3.9.2+ (Build: 20201002) installation in Administration> Server >Tasks: "Server->Task-> tool_cohortroles\task\cohort_role_sync  after 'Run now': "Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort Execute scheduled task: Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort (tool_cohortroles\task\cohort_role_sync) ... started 15:36:22. Current memory use 13.4MB. Sync cohort roles... ... used 4 dbqueries ... used 0.012479066848755 seconds Scheduled task failed: Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort (tool_cohortroles\task\cohort_role_sync) An encoding error has been detected, needs to be reviewed by a programmer scheduled: User ID does not exist or is deleted!"" In Administration>Server>Tasks this task has been run daily whit result: "Error" from a month! Please help me to troubleshoot this situation. I don't know if any user is affected and how. Someone know a workaround for this? I appreciate a step-by-step explanation. Thank you in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort - cohort_role_sync
ResponsesInList.Text: This is your clue: "User ID does not exist or is deleted!" So, it is trying to process a user in a cohort whose id is not there any more. So, if you turn on cron debugging, then you should be able to get the details of exactly which user that is and take a look into fixing it. See the documentation on Debugging for how to set up the cron debugging output: https://docs.moodle.org/310/en/Debugging

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort - cohort_role_sync
ResponsesInList.Text: How can I find the "userid= number->xy" to delete it's reference in Moodle/DB? The user IS deleted by an Anonimity Plugin, but the reference at it is saved somewhere in MySQL DB and every task that runs "cohort_role_sync" gave the error that I pasted above.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Synchronize the role assignments of the cohort - cohort_role_sync
ResponsesInList.Text: When you "delete" a user in Moodle, it sets the value in the "deleted" column in the user table to 1. All the various processes in Moodle then know to skip this user as deleted. Not all the user data is actually deleted, but some may be retained. In any case, it will not throw any errors for standard Moodle. I do not know of a plugin by that name, but that's where the trouble lies. If it actually removed the user from the table but did not clean up all the references to the user in other places, then it did a bad job, since clearly there are still references to it in the cohort members lists.

ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 3.8.5+ (Build: 20201103) I created an observer role called Registrar and assigned the role at the category level because I want the registrars to be able to view everything in our category of for-credit courses, but not other categories of courses.  The 2 users who are assigned the role of Registrar only have the additional role of Authenticated User--they are not Students. When I look at the Participants list in one of the for-credit courses, the Registrars are listed in the role "registrar."  I thought this was okay.  But I just found out that they are also showing up in the gradebook.  A professor alerted me that when he was grading an assignment, the registrars were listed as if they were students who needed an assignment graded. Questions: 1. Is it actually correct that the Registrars show up on the Participants list? 2.  How do I fix the fact they they are showing up like enrolled students? Thanks, Michele

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why is observer role is enrolled in course?
ResponsesInList.Text: In case anyone else gets into this situation, I discovered that I had enabled "Category enrolment" at Site admin > Plugins > Enrolments. This told Moodle to enroll the people assigned at the category level, which added the Registrars to the "Enrolled users" on the course's Participants list. When I disabled "Category enrolment," the Registrars were added to the "Other Users" in the course's Participants list, meaning that they were not enrolled but had some permissions in the course. That is what I wanted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why is observer role is enrolled in course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Good troubleshooting there For other with similar issues, then answer to the questions above is 1) Yes, category level roles will show up on the Participants list in Moodle, but only as roles that trickle down, like Manager does, for instance. They are "particpants" in the course by virtue of their role in a higher context , but are not enrolled. If the are actually enrolled and should not be, then 2) you fix this by looking at the user details in the Participants list to find out out exactly what enrolment method has put them in the course, where which is where you should go to fix it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course categories don't show anymore in Course settings
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Toms, For other course categories to show in the Course category select menu, the teacher must have the "Change course category" capability in these other categories. Normally, a user is assigned the role of teacher in a course and not a category context , hence only the current course category is displayed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course categories don't show anymore in Course settings
ResponsesInList.Text: I just want to mention that I found a solution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course categories don't show anymore in Course settings [Solved]
ResponsesInList.Text: Well done for figuring out a solution and thanks for posting it! As you've found, the "Change course category" capability must be given to a teacher by assigning them a role, either in a category context, or as a system role (then all course categories on the site are shown in the select menu).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course categories don't show anymore in Course settings [Solved]
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Helen! How can I do just that by only changing the teacher role without creating an additional role? I've tried checking the System and Category checkboxes in the teacher profile, but teachers still cannot change the category of their courses. Regards, Thomas

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course categories don't show anymore in Course settings [Solved]
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Thomas, The System and Category checkboxes on the edit role page are for allowing the role to be assigned in these contexts. Normally the Teacher role is assigned in the course context i.e. you enrol a teacher in the course and give them the role of Teacher. You can assign teachers the role of Teacher in the system context by going to Site administration / Users / Permissions / Assign system roles. However, they would then have the role of Teacher in every course on your site. This is most likely not what you want! Thus, you would need to create an additional role, as described in the documentation Capabilities/moodle/course:changecategory .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't remove Assigned system roles
ResponsesInList.Text:
Stefan, As Tue says, they are greyed out because they were created by the LDAP component and not by you or another administrator. It knows this because of the component name and the modifierid that is saved in the row for that entry in the role_assignments table. When this is shown on the screen, the code greys this out since you are not that component or modifier who created it and don't have the rights to change it. If you run the query he posted, it will show you this. Or, you can use this query in the Config Reports or Ad-hoc database plugin to show you all the system level role assignments, with extra data to show you which row each entry has in the role_assignments table. SELECT u.username AS "User", r.shortname AS "Role", ra.id AS "Role_assignments id", ra.component, (SELECT username FROM prefix_user WHERE id = ra.modifierid) AS "Modifier" FROM prefix_role_assignments ra JOIN prefix_role r ON r.id = ra.roleid JOIN prefix_user u ON u.id = ra.userid # system level only WHERE ra.contextid = 1 (Note: You can use this any SQL tool of course as long as you change the
"prefix_ "marker before the table names to your actual prefix such as
mdl_). The "Role assignments id" is the id number of the row in the role_ssignments table for that user's role assignment. The component is blank for normal role assignments done by hand. If a plugin or other component created the role, its name will be there. To fix this you can: 1) Edit the row and change the component to a blank and change the modifierid to your own user id as the admin. This should then allow you to remove the user using the interface in Assign system roles. or 2) Delete the row. This is actually what the Assign system roles does when you remove someone from a role manually: it removes the whole role from the table. Good luck. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: coursecreator in course context
ResponsesInList.Text: Leonard, This is the way it works. When a user has a role at the system level, such as Manager or Course creator, and are also enrolled in a course in a course level role, then the Participants list in the course shows both the system level roles and the course level roles. This is useful in case you have a system level role and a course level role that may conflict on certain permissions and you need to troubleshoot the issue. For example, you may have a system level role that allows someone to see but not edit grades and this is not working properly when they are also a teacher in the course. You want to be able to see what roles are "above" the course at the system level since those permissions are inherited. In the case of the standard Course creator role, this is a system level / category level role only - by defintion. It would make no sense to have a Course creator role at the Course level since you have to be outside of the course to create a new course. There is no conflict of permissions in this case between Course creator and Teacher. Everything is working fine, as you say. So, the teacher is not "marked as course creator for that course" -- what you are seeing is the system level role being inherited and shown in the Participants list. I hope this is clear.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "Editingteacher" can not delete message
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ricardo, The reason why the teacher can't delete the message is because the user has the role of teacher in the course context , whereas the capability to delete any messages on the site needs to allowed for a role assigned in the system context. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Precedence of roles in the "Define roles" screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, this ordering is only for display. The way capabilities are done in code is to check for a specific capability directly, not for the role. In fact, checking for roles in code is poor practice: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Access_API#Determining_that_a_user_has_a_given_capability . In case of permission conflicts on the same capability in the same context inherited from multiple roles, there is a numerical weighting system to calculate the correct permissions when capabilities conflict. There's documentation on it somewhere I can't find at the moment, but this "tie-breaker" system is based on capabilities/permissions not on the role.

ResponsesInList.Title: How can I bulk-assign system roles to existing moodle accounts?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there! We have a Moodle site that we need to bulk assign existing LDAP users a system role. Our users are enrolled via SOAP UI messages from our enrolment platform. I've got a spreadsheet of over 1000 employees (email address and full name) to update, but I cannot confirm if all have logged into the system (to create the local account in Moodle). I am aware that Moodle has a bulk edit feature , but I don't want to use this in case it creates manual Moodle accounts for users it cannot locate, as this won't connect the Moodle account via LDAP and with the SOAP UI messages coming through. With this in mind, how can I bulk update these users with the system role required?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bulk-assign system roles to existing moodle accounts?
ResponsesInList.Text: You can do this using the standard Upload users tool and assign them any system level role you have created. Details are here: https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Upload_users#Set_system_roles . Just be sure to use the shortname of the custom role you have created, and when you do the upload, set the type of processing to "Update existing users only" since this is LDAP and the accounts already exist.

ResponsesInList.Title: High level role on a user contextlevel?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I was doing a routine check on my roles and I ran a query that showed me that there was an instructor who had a role manager in the context level 30. According to Moodle, that context level is "another user". I would like to find where this was granted and how can I remove it but I have no idea. I checked the instructor course enrollments and that manager role doesn't appear there. Can someone shed light on this? Best, Fabian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: High level role on a user contextlevel?
ResponsesInList.Text: Fabian, The the most common use of user to user context assignment is the Parent or Mentor role explained here: https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Parent_role . That's a typical way to set one up. What differs in such roles is the specific capabilities they have; the method of assigning a user to user role will always be the same. To find out what is happening on your site: First, the place where a user is a assigned to another user is on the user profile of target user in the Preferences > Roles > Assign roles relative to this user. So take a look on the profile of the instructor user in your situation to see what other role and person(s) has been assigned to them there. Secondly, this can only happen if you have defined a custom role (or messed with a standard role) so that it is able to be be assigned in the User context. Check in Site admin > Users > Permissions > Define roles and see if any of the roles there are able to be assigned in a user context. You will find that information on the definition page for every role in the "Context types where this role may be assigned" setting where the User checkbox is checked. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: High level role on a user contextlevel?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Randy, That was very useful. Indeed, I have historically inherited a custom role that was apparently a clone of manager role, which had the ability to be assigned in user, course, category, and system contexts. I removed the ability to assign it in user and course context and the problem disappeared; security review passes now Thank you! Best, Fabian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: High level role on a user contextlevel?
ResponsesInList.Text: Fabian, Ah, excellent! I have never seen anyone do this with the Manager role, that is interesting. There must have been some situation where that was useful - or they were just trying it out. Anyway, glad it is fixed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hide some plugins for a specific role
ResponsesInList.Text: My understanding is that the Administrator role is handled differently from other roles. Basically, there is no set of permissions for the Admin role - if a user has that role, then TRUE is always returned when they get checked for permissions. There is no matrix of individual capabilities for a user with that role. That is, you cannot select an "Administrator archetype" and just remove a couple capabilities. The closest default role to what you're looking for is the Manager role, but that role usually does not have permission to edit most plugins, for example, so you would need to significantly modify the role (Allow a lot of capabilities) to make it feel like an Administrator. Consider that, if they had permission to do everything besides editing those two plugins, they would have permission to change their role and add that capability back. So, you could try to also remove the capability to modify roles, but if they need pseudo-Admin privileges, then this could hinder their ability to troubleshoot other kinds of problems. At this point, it is starting to feel kind of messy. All that said, I am sure you are not the first person to need an almost-Admin or super-Manager, so perhaps someone else has a similar role preset they can share. I imagine such a role would require a bit of upkeep any time you upgraded Moodle or added a new plugin (adding new capabilities). I don't want to tell you what to do, since I know very little about your situation, but if you intend to give them privileges to do anything else on your site (see user personal information, modify grades, delete courses, change sitewide settings, etc.), it's hard to understand what is so special about those two plugins, in comparison. If you could describe the requirement a little more, it could help put it in context and possibly lead to a solution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: List of users assigned category-level roles (site-wide)
ResponsesInList.Text:
If you install https://moodle.org/plugins/report_customsql then 
```text
SELECT


    cc.id AS categoryid,


    cc.name AS categoryname,


    r.shortname AS role,


    u.username,


    u.firstname,


    u.lastname,


    u.email




FROM mdl_user u


JOIN mdl_role_assignments ra ON ra.userid = u.id
```

ResponsesInList.Text: Mario, Yes, partly. What you need to do is remove the ability of the Manager role to assign the Teacher role to anyone. So, in Define roles, edit the Manager role, and on the tab called "Allow role assignments," uncheck the Teacher role. This means a Manager can not assign anyone (including themselves) as a Teacher. When you assign this role in the usual way as the Manager of a Category to someone, they will not be able to assign the Teacher role for courses under that Category (they can assign the other roles, like Student etc.) Now, this will also prevent them from assigning other users as a Teacher as well. So, if you need to have them  enrol others as Teachers, but not enrol themselves, then I don't think there is a solution because there is no specific capability in the system for "enrol yourself" that you could prevent (but there are a couple for "unenrol self" ones). Of course, the above example changes the main Manager role. In real life, I would not do that, instead I would clone the Manager role to a new role called something like Manager-not-teacher, then change that Allow role setting for, and assign such users to that new role and assign it to them at the Category level. That would leave the normal Manager role intact as is. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing managers from enrolling themselves in a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Mario, Right, I thought that might be your situation. I'm not sure that is possible from what I see. The tab for "Allow role assignments" controls whether a particular role can assign those various roles to anyone: it's an all or nothing, everyone or no one setting. So basically, if they can enrol others, they can enrol themselves. If not, then not. And, as I mentioned, there does not seem to be any specific capability related to "enrol self" as opposed to "other others" but rather just one to allow to enrol anyone. What is your goal? Are you combing this with the prevention of seeing Quizzes & Questions? Such that a Manager will not be able to enrol themselves as a Teacher to get around that limitation from the Manager without quizzes role? If so, then a possible solution is in the Manager with no quizzes role, you can set those permissions for the Quiz and Question from Not Set or Prevent to Prohibit. Prohibit will not allow the permissions from another role to override those. In that case, even if the Manager enrols themselves as a Teacher, the Prohibit permissions will win the permission conflict. If that is what you are after, give that a try.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Account Preferences
ResponsesInList.Text: Eric, 1) "When they log in, however, the only option under "User account" is "Change password". "This tells us immediately that your default role of Authenticated user has been changed, as all authenticated users by default are allowed to edit their own profile via the capability moodle/user:editownprofile. See https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Capabilities/moodle/user:editownprofile . 2) Similarly, there is an explicit capability named "Edit own user messaging profile" moodle/user:editownmessageprofile which when set to Allow enables a user to set their Messaging and Notification preferences (even if they don't have the right to edit the rest of their profile). This also is set to allow by default. See this page https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Capabilities/moodle/user:editownmessageprofile for a couple of links to how to solve this issue if you want to prevent students from setting it and only allow faculty. But basically, in your case, seeing that the role 'Authenticated user' has those turned off already, you can set up a system wide role that has just one capability editownmessageprofile set to Allow, then assign your faculty users to that role. Randy

Different default site settings can be stored in file /local/defaults.php.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sys admin access dissapeared?!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Avoid editing the database if you can!! When you’re logged in as you, look at /user/profile.php - you will see a “id=nnn” at the end of the url, where nnn is a number. Try adding this towards the end of config.php (not right at the end - make sure the `?>` is the last thing in that file!!) 
```text
$CFG=>siteadmins='nnn';
```
 If you need more site admins, you can comma-separate the id numbers, eg: 
```text
$CFG=>siteadmins='nnn,aaa,bbb,ccc';
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sys admin access dissapeared?!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sys admin access dissapeared?!
ResponsesInList.Text: Well it’s as temporary or as permanent as you wish - it will remain until you change that line in the config file. The config file allows you to lock values for certain settings - see your config-dist.php file for all the options. The usual advantage is that that file overrides the database settings, preventing them from being “messed about with”. That allows hosting providers or IT departments the ability to establish various setting without worrying about users/admins being able to change them. The disadvantage is that you can’t override them via the Moodle admin interface so it relies on a level of tech support that some people just don’t have. Whatever works best for your needs

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Separate groups for non-editing teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: That sounds like a valid an useful use-case. However, I am afraid that the current Moodle versions do not support that. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a role that can Create/modify students but not edit materials
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, I'd suggest you start with the manager role and remove all permissions related to editing courses or grading. An easy way to figure out which permissions you need would be to use our Moodle sandbox demo and log in as an admin in one browser and as a manager in another browser. You can then use the admin account to edit the manager role and use the manager account to test the changes. (You just need to refresh the page for any permissions changes to be shown for the manager account.) The Moodle sandbox demo sites resets every hour on the hour, so a good plan is to start just after the hourly reset to give yourself plenty of time. Once you are happy with your customised manager role, you can export it from the Moodle sandbox demo site and then import it in your own Moodle site.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Configuring a Supervisor role
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rebekah As far as I know, the Assignment module's capability to grade (mod/assign:grade) is evaluated in the context of the module, not the participant. So all your supervisors will need it to be able to grade submitted essays. If essays are submitted via the Quiz module, the setup should be similar. To make sure that a supervisor is able to assess only their engineers and noone else, you can try to use groups. The idea is, you would set up groups, each group having one supervisor and all her/his engineers. With separate group mode of the activity set, it should work that the supervisors can see only the members of their own group (because you would not give permission to access all groups). In other words, for the purposes of assessments, your supervisors should have https://docs.moodle.org/en/Non-editing_teacher_role in the given activities.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Configuring a Supervisor role
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd second this...though I don't know that you'd need a plug-in...I've been doing something like it for years without (but then, I'm used to doing stuff the hard way, so...). Create the cohort, add all your users (including supervisors).  Create the groups in a csv spreadsheet (excel, column A row 1 called groupname.  That's it...list all your group names in column A under the header, save as csv). Import the csv to each course.  Cohort sync enroll to each course, adding to the group on cohort enrollment.  I would then make sure to give your supervisors the extra (Supervisor) role they need.  If someone changes teams, you change their cohort (put them in the new cohort first, then remove them from the old, you might check to remove them from the old groups, though).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teachers unable to send messages to students - Sorry, but you do not currently have permissions to do that (Send messages to any user)
ResponsesInList.Text: To clarify, the user must have the capability "moodle/site:sendmessage" on the system context . There are multiple ways to control this. Granting this capability for the Authenticated user gives it to everyone. If you want to allow messaging to staff only, create a new role such as "Message sender" with the capability enabled (and unset it from all other roles). Assign the new role at Site administration > Users > Permissions > Assign system roles to staff members only. You can't simply use the Teacher role for this as that one is typically assigned on lower course level context, not globally. See e.g. https://docs.moodle.org/en/Context#Roles_and_contexts for details.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign different roles per person per group in the same course
ResponsesInList.Text: No, it is not possible. Roles can be assigned in a particular context only and groups are not a context. Enrolled users have particular role in the context of the course and can have eventually different role in the context of individual activity modules in the course. So your student "S" could have a role "Student" in the course "C" and role "Teacher" in some particular activity - such as Assignment or Forum within the course. But group membership does not affect roles. Maybe you can try and describe what you want to achieve from a pedagogical / teaching / learning perspective, there might be some alternative solutions. HTH

ResponsesInList.Title: The difference between role_assignments and user_enrollments tables
ResponsesInList.Text: Revisiting a lot of my old SQL reports and updating them for Moodle 3.4, I am wondering what is the actual difference between (mdl_)role_assignments and (mdl_)user_enrollments tables, and when it is best to use them in reports. I have looked into the code (functions and APIs), the Moodle developer docs, these forums and ask Google too, but with not so much success Dear Moodle HQ and developers, your help is appreciated BTW , when coding is concerned, I am using the ROLE or ACCESS API, of course and not those tables directly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The difference between role_assignments and user_enrollments tables
ResponsesInList.Text: My understanding: The enrolments system is best used to check if somebody 'belongs' to a course. Usually this would mean you are a student, teacher, or other member of staff specifically related to that course. The role assignments are used to control permissions on that course. I think you can probably have role assignments even if you don't have an enrolment. You can also have roles in a parent context which might affect permissions on the course. Obviously, you can have multiple roles on a course, and there may be many custom roles with different permissions in a Moodle system. Fundamentally in terms of user access, it all depends on your role assignments and not enrolments, with one exception (this is a summary from memory - I am leaving out logic relating to hidden courses etc). In order to access a course you need to EITHER have moodle/course:view OR be enrolled in the course. So basically, do you want to list everyone in a course? -> use enrolments (but be aware that there will be some people, like system admin and maybe others, who can access the course without being on that list). Do you want to check if somebody has access to something? -> use role assignments/capabilities (but in some cases you might also need to take enrolment into account). Not sure if I covered everything here...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The difference between role_assignments and user_enrollments tables
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Sam! that makes a lot of sense to me, and reassures  most of what I was already imagined about it. now, it feel more solidified As I was initially looking for a formal Moodle HQ answer in the developer wiki, now I am Looking for the proper place to add that information, and maybe add some SQL queries to support it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The difference between role_assignments and user_enrollments tables
ResponsesInList.Text: My understanding of this is that user_enrolments asserts only that a person is enrolled on a course, without any notion of what role or permissions they have on that course. On the other hand, role_assignments is not specific to courses and defines what roles users hold at different security contexts. I guess if your reports are about users on a course in any way you would join to user_enrolments, and if you need further information on what roles they have in the course you can also join to role_assignments.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles that can edit only users that were added by that user
ResponsesInList.Text: How smart is it to do some custom modifications It depends on how those changes are made and what are your skills in development and patches management. In general: If you do not need to customize, then do not customize. If you need a custom feature, try to achieve it by a plugin without changing the Moodle core. If you need to change the Moodle core, do it wisely: minimise changes, keep it well isolated, maintain a custom git branch, do not alter core DB tables and APIs. It is important to realize that any such change is not a one-time task. It is not a thing you do once and use it forever. You will have to look after every such change. Re-apply it on the next upgrade, re-test it, deal with eventual conflicts with upstream changes and so on.

I have groups of users who have different capabilities and can only take certain classes where other students can take all classes, and then I have other groups that can take a category of classes but not other categories.  So for example: I have courses by Category as follows: iPhone (category) - Intro to iPhone (class) - how to install apps (class) Android (category) - making the switch (class) Windows Mobile (category) - Intro to Windows 10 mobile (class) Scenarios Student 1 - can only work with iPhone so only needs this category Student 2 - can only work with Android so only needs this category Student 3 - can work with iPhone and Android needs both categories Student 4 - can work with all categories - phone, android, and windows Now imagine I have these different students but not just 4 students by several hundred all having one of these permission requirements. and what I am confused about is how to set up groups and then subsequent permissions by these class examples I noted above. What I really want to do is define this hierarchy such as: iPhone Resellers - only see iPhone classes Android Resellers - only see Android classes Super Reseller - people who can sell both iPhone and Android Is it possible to set up Cohorts (I believe is what I want) by classes and then when I enroll a new user I determine what Reseller group (Cohort) they below to and they then automatically get both enrolled and have access to the classes they are supposed to see.  But all other classes remain hidden from them. Is this possible?  I am using moodle 3.4x Much appreciate your guidance and help on how to configure this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles, Permissions and Groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! Yes, "Cohort sync" enrolment method is what you need (be careful and avoid using cohorts from the manual enrolment method... because you want the users will be enrolled automatically to the courses when there're added to a cohort!) You'll find all the information about the "Cohort sync" on this page: https://docs.moodle.org/34/en/Cohort_sync#Enrolling_a_cohort_in_a_course Please, let us to know if you have some more question Kind regards!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles, Permissions and Groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sara, Thanks for your help and No I had not done this at the course level and just "found" where course administration was to even add this!  LOL So on this path the dialog asks for an instance name and to create a new group or none. So What's the instance name used for - would you name it the same as the course or the cohort? and do I really need to create groups if I am using Cohorts? You see in the scenario I painted I basically am trying to keep the different groups segmented so they can only get into the classes they are authorized for and that's it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles, Permissions and Groups
ResponsesInList.Text: As Sara says, yes to cohorts assigning to courses.  That's the easiest.  Making courses they aren't eligible for hidden is probably not possible--but they won't be able to take them (unless you set open self-enrollment). I'd add some course description that is clear who the courses are for. So cohorts: Go to the area you want the cohorts and create your cohorts--If the levels won't changes, you can create them at the site level (Site Administration->Users->Cohorts) but if you set up courses by year, you might need to create cohorts at the category level instead (Category settings->Cohorts. Example: X group of people has to take A-C courses and Y group takes J-H courses in 2017 and X group takes D-E courses and y group take K-N courses in 2018 but some people change groups between 2017 and 2018. Once the cohorts are created, you'll add all the people to each one.  Go to each course, add cohort sync enrollment method (as Sara described) for each cohort (iPhone Resellers would have a cohort sync enrollment method and so would Super Resellers and Ultimate Resellers in the iPhone classes; The Android Resellers would have a cohort sync enrollment method in the Android classes and so would the Super and Ultimate resellers. Three methods per class).  As new staff are hired, you'll just add them to the appropriate cohort and they will be added to the course. If you want groups added to the courses to be able to look at each cohort separately in the reports, you can create groups and when you add the cohort sync, select the group and they'll be added immediately. Groups have to be created in each course (but you could set up a csv upload and just load them that way).

ResponsesInList.Text: So I believe I figured this between you both!!! So I went back and unenrolled all 4 test students to start from all four classes. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles in Enroll course not working well, How to reset all default roles?
ResponsesInList.Text: Rule on Roles: (my rules that I have always implemented. 1. Only Site Admins are assigned this Role at Site Level. NO OTHER USER is given a Role here except for default "Authenticated User" Role. Addendum: Staff Members can be given a variation of the Authenticated User Role but allowing them to see hidden files. DO NOT use any other Role as the template for this Role, DO NOT allow any other Capability ONLY "View Hidden Files". 2. Course Creators and Managers are assigned Roles at Category or Sub-Category Level. 3. Teachers, Non-Editing Teachers and Students given Roles at Course level. 4. Guests are never allowed access to any course not set on the Front Page for Guests to access. 5. All other Roles, e.g. Mentor or Parent are assigned at Course Level ONLY I have always used this guide and it has never failed me. The only time I have had Role issues is when someone else has set Roles at the Site Level. _________________________________ I suspect your Course Creator Role is set at Site Level which is why there is no Delete icon. Course Creators should not be able to access courses they create, unless they enrol themselves as Teacher, never as Student. Course Creators should ALWAYS enroll someone as a Teacher then leave that course and not return as Course Creator. I know that is a pain, occasionally, but the Teacher has more editing capabilities than a Course Creator, (from memory so may not be correct). If you want your Manager to act as a Course Creator, then  make sure they have all the required permissions. No one should be enrolled in a course as Course Creator, so check your Roles in Site Admin > Users > Permissions > Define Roles and Allow Role Assignments. This is what mine looks like: No one below the Role of Teacher can assign Roles. There is, occasionally, an issue with Teachers not being able to assign a Teacher's Role to someone else, but this is easily worked around by discussion with the Manager or an Admin.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest Access Not Working
ResponsesInList.Text: Lauren, When you say 'the course does not show up' do you mean that the course is not visible to the Guest user in the list of courses at all? The Guest should be able to see the list of courses after login. So check the course is visible and the category is visible too. The usual order of things I check for with Guest issues is: - User policies - are Visitor and Guest set to the Guest role? - User policies - is auto login on or off ? (It should work either way, just behave differently given a link) - Is Appearance > Allow guest to use Dashboard on or off? (should work either way,just behave differently; when off it should redirect to the home page) - Is Plugins > Enrolment > Guest access actually really enabled ? - Is the Show button on in Authentication? (Definitely is in your case) - Is the Guest access enrollment method added to the course and also is it really enabled? By default, guest is logged in the standard log as well, so that is also a possible source of information for troubleshooting. - Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can students see their mentors?
ResponsesInList.Text:
For the curious, here is a Configurable Reports query to show the user who runs it who their Mentors are. Tested in M 3.4. It assumes you have a role with the shortname 'mentor' though you can change that to any such role name, like 'parent'. This is based the original query by Tim Hunt in this thread: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=199269#p880308 
```text
SELECT 


CONCAT(u.firstname ,' ',u.lastname) AS 'My Mentor(s)'


FROM prefix_user u


JOIN prefix_role_assignments ra ON ra.userid = u.id


JOIN prefix_role role ON role.id = ra.roleid


JOIN prefix_context ctx ON ctx.id = ra.contextid AND ctx.contextlevel = 30


JOIN prefix_user me ON me.id = ctx.instanceid


WHERE role.shortname = 'mentor' 


AND me.id = %%USERID%%
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling/Allowing access to Plagiarism Plugins for certain Teachers

If you don't want the 40 teachers inadvertently using unicheck in all their courses, it would be best to only assign them the "unicheck teacher" role in the 10 courses. If you don't want to do this manually (going into each of the 10 courses), you could use the feature Upload users or Flat file .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling/Allowing access to Plagiarism Plugins for certain Teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Helen, This is exactly what I have done - the only slight difference is that all of the teachers were already enrolled with the standard teacher role on their respective courses. For future reference: I created a new role called "unicheck teacher" based on the standard teacher role. For standard teachers I did not allow any unicheck options (apart from viewing existing plagiarism reports). For Unicheck I allowed all options. Standard teachers simply don't even see any options for unicheck when creating assignments so it is now impossible for them to accidentally add this as an option. It was actually much quicker than I thought to add the additional role (which over-rides) existing roles because all of the teachers already had enrolments in their courses as teachers. By filtering the users list just by teachers, clicking to add additional roles for applicable teachers was very fast and took less than five minutes for all of the courses. The upload users and flat file options would probably be very useful if I needed to assign the role to more than 40 teachers but in this case it was actually quick to do it manually. I was hoping that there would be an option to combine cohorts and roles to speed up the maintenance of this each year but obviously that's not possible at the moment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Role with no notifications
ResponsesInList.Text: Casey, My experience is every module does notifications differently, has different code. There's no central control or management of it. It's an inconsistent mess. For Assignment, it sends notifications by checking the mod/assign:receivegradernotifications permission . This is set to Allow for Teacher and non-editing teacher by default, but then you can set it off per assignment. Set that to prevent (or prohibit if you have to) for your custom role. That one should work. For Quiz, there are no such useful activity level settings and the permission for it  , mod/quiz:emailnotifysubmission, is not set for any roles by default (??). I imagine you have tried that one and maybe it worked or not. For Feedback, there are no activity settings either but there is the capability mod/feedback:receivemail which is allowed by default for the two teacher roles. For other items, similarly, it just depends on whether there is any setting or permission to control the notification.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher can no more reset a course after update
ResponsesInList.Text: I found how to solve that problem while doing 2 verifications : I had a look at the permissions of one teacher in a course while consulting the following menu : ADMINISTRATION > Course administration > Users > Permissions > Check permissions I saw that this teacher was not authorized to reset courses (while the teacher profile was well authorized to). I had a look at the capacity overview report in site administration : ADMINISTRATION > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Capability overview I searched for the "course:reset" capability for all roles. And I found the authenticated user column to indicate the reset:cours actions to be forbidden ! I did not find how to modify the forbidden "course:reset" capability of authenticated user through admin interface, but I found how to do it trough database : find the authenticated user id in mdl_role table search for that roleid in mdl_role_capabilities table, with capability  %like% course:reset verify this line has a " permission " column to "-1000" delete this line Verify your capability overview report and verify your teacher role can reset courses ! Important to remember in case of capability problem : have a look at the Capability overview report though ADMINISTRATION > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Capability overview Select all roles, and it will help you to understand how to solve the problem. Note that our Moodle is a very old instance, and this hopefully explains while we encounter such problems. Zabelle

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manager or teachers (we call AOD Trainers) cannot enrol and assign roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Mata, So, if the Trainee is just a renaming of the standard Student role, then that is probably not the issue. A couple of things: 1) Going back to the screenshot of your settings, you will notice that there are more things there than in the default ones, as in the screenshot that Helen has. For instance, a Trainer can assign Managers in a course, which is not a good thing. And course creator has all sorts of role assigning power it does not need and should not have. Also, notice that the Authenticated user column, where four roles can assign that. That is not needed and may cause issues. In other words, there are a lot of odd things on this screen which need to be cleared up first so you can eliminate those as possible sources of the problem. Basically, setting aside the Enrolment Manager one, those other roles are standard and so this screen should resemble the default screen shown in  Helen's screenshot. In general, it's a best practice not to assign users multiple roles at the site level unless absolutely needed, because the various permissions of the multiple roles can collide and do unexpected things. That is the first thing I would clear up: regularize that page. You need to simply those settings to eliminate potential role conflict issues. 2) Next, I would test the roles themselves by isolating them: a) Enrolling a test user account who has NO other site wide role at all except Authenticated user into a course in the AOD Trainer role. If it works, then issue is probably due to the conflict of roles and assignments thing and not to the specific capabilities and permissions of the role. b) If it does not work, then I next suspect the role capabilities and to test that I would create a new Test Teacher role from scratch based on the Teacher archteype. I would enroll a test user who has NO other site level role at all to be the Test Teacher in a course. If that solves the issue, then the source of the problem is in the difference between Teacher archetype and the AOD Trainer role you have. (I usually analyze such issues by exporting both roles into their XML files and the comparing the two files in a text editor because staring at those screens is not healthy. However you can also obviously use the Capability overview tool in Site admin > Users> Permissions as well. ) If you have changed nothing but the names, then all those other settings should be the same. 3) Sanity checks I am sure you have also done a sanity check for your enrollment methods, that they are on and have no weird things like dates. Another sanity check is that the issue not just that pull down menu. So, I would go into the course as AOD Trainer, and in Users > Enrolment methods > Manual enrolments, click the people icon in the Edit column. This should bring up a left-right two column picking screen. Can you enrol users here? Does the pull down here work? If so, then issue is theme or interface related rather than role definitions.  (That would be super obscure, but that's why we do sanity checks ;) Hope this is helpful. - Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Allowing Course Creators to edit/manage all Courses

Chris, That is really what the Manager role is for: to edit/manage all courses on the site. The Course creator role is extremely specific in function: it has only one additional function over a normal user, to create a course and to be put into it as Teacher. It has no other special abilities. If the Manager role does too much for what you need, then it is much
easier to remove abilities from the Manager role than add all the ones
you would need to the Course creator role to get all the various course management abilities. One thing Managers can not do is create new courses. ResponsesInList.Title: This issue will blow your mind!
ResponsesInList.Text: I have created a guest account with guest permissions and enrolled in 2 shells but this guest account seemed to be enrolled in other shells too and when I check the account profile, the other shell names are not listed but only the ones I enrolled them to. So, how is this even possible that guest is able to access shells that he is not enrolled in? Blows my mind! Please see role settings attached. Moodle 3.04 Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: This issue will blow your mind!
ResponsesInList.Text: Your question is really about two different things:  Roles and Accounts Roles determine what permission someone has if they are assigned it in specific contexts.  These are assigned to individual accounts. Accounts represent people.  They are what you (or a user) will log into. If you say a role is available at the system level, a user can be given that permission for the entire site...for every course and category in the site. Your image above says the guest role can be enrolled at the system level (in everything).  If the guest account is assigned as guest role at the system level, it will act like the account is enrolled in everything, even though the courses won't acknowledge it as actual enrollment (look at the Other roles section of Users in a course--that's where they'll show up), the account will be able to access all courses but probably won't actually be able to participate properly because most activities /resources require you to actually have a course role to use them (system roles don't count as course roles). In old Moodle (1.9 and before) the student role was available at all levels.  I had a lot of people give category and system level student roles to our staff and then the crying and moaning started.  Because category and system roles aren't...well, best word I've got is REAL.  The courses won't recognize them as students and won't give grades or allow some participation. This is bad. In Moodle 2.X and above, the student role was by default only available at the course level which simplified a lot of stuff.  Some people have complained about the change but it was a positive move.  No more accidentally screwing people up.  Now you have to do it on purpose. System roles are really for admins, managers, people who need to access all courses for management reasons.  Category roles are for those people who need access to all courses in that category and below, also for management reasons.  Course roles are for participation and teaching.  A teacher role at a category level cannot do all of the same things in a course that a teacher role in a specific course can. Roles require a lot of attention to detail and big picture thinking.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: This issue will blow your mind!
ResponsesInList.Text: First:  Go to one of the courses they should not have access to but do.  Rather than clicking on Users->Enrolled Users, click on Users->Other users.  Based on what you said, you will most likely see the users in this area with this information in the Roles area (on the right):  Guest (assigned at site level). Second:  Go to Site Administration->Users->Permissions->Assign system roles.  Click on the Guest role.  You most likely have given all your students the guest role, which isn't actual enrollment but allows access to everything.  Remove them. If you want someone to have the guest role in a course, set the course to allow guests. (Course Administration->Edit Settings-> Guest Access.  Change the setting to yes.  If you want them to have to enter a password to use guest access, add a password. Save

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Allow Admin to only add accounts to courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Last question first:  Administrator isn't a role, per se (it's a way of life).  It is assigned in a different way and you can't copy it.  You either are or you aren't.  It is assigned in Site Administration->Users->Permissions-> Site administrators (rather than assign system roles). First question:  It is all about permissions.  I'm still on 2.8, so the permissions may vary slightly (they haven't changed a lot since about 2.3 as far as I can tell, but they could have changed a little.  There are a lot of permissions.  Sometimes you have to experiment a bit (I like to keep two browsers open...one logged in as Admin to mess with the role and one logged in as the role I'm fiddling with).  Some permissions only work when another is allowed...or when a role is at a particular level (I want my trainers to be able to move their courses...but that is a permission which only works at the site level, which means either they can move any course or they can't move any course...I can't change where they can move them...scary!). You probably want to remove permission to view others' grades, view course reports, overview reports (okay, all Grades reports), view course logs, view activity reports, view activity completion reports, allowing grading in any activity (there are a bunch), allowing deleting of attempts of any type in any activity. You probably want to allow permission to configure enrollment instances (maybe), view participants (you have to see them to add them in the course), assign roles to users. There may be more...Maybe take a look at non-editing teacher...it might be closer to what you're looking for.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk Unenrol

On another tack about enrollments, I too used to complain about the Moodle 2 system, but having got to grips with it recently I can say that it's a lot better than the old one. Basically, Moodle separates two disctinct processes which were muddled together in 1.9, that is, authentication -- how users login to the system -- and course enrollments -- how they get enrolled into a course. It also makes explicit the method by which a user is enrolled -- the enrollment 'method'. Once you've got the hang of this it's a lot easier to figure out what to do for a given circumstance. The system is actually more forgiving than it used to be -- for example, we have automated (kind of) enrollments with the Banner Luminis Message broker (LMB) but I can also manually enroll a student and if LMB subsequently adds that user again it merely duplicates the enrollment to no ill effect. I think that some of the problems that people have is that the Participants interface shows some of the same information as Enrolled Users but not all. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: View profile not allowed
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alfredo, You're correct in thinking that viewing a full profile (as opposed to a course profile) is permissions-related. You're also correct in thinking that it's to do with the capability moodle/user:viewdetails. The reason why an administrator can view a full profile is because they have a system role and so have the capability moodle/user:viewdetails at system level. A teacher normally has the role of teacher at course level (they are assigned the role of teacher in a particular course) and so have the capability moodle/user:viewdetails at course level only. This means that they can see course profiles but not full profiles. If you want everyone on your site to be able to view full profiles, you can simply allow moodle/user:viewdetails for the authenticated user role (as we do here on moodle.org). If you only want teachers to be able to view full profiles (in addition to admins and managers), you will need to create a custom role, as explained in the documentation Capabilities/moodle/user:viewdetails .
